Generally speaking it is the Pilot's final decision on how much fuel the aircraft is loaded with. Pilots Will based their decision based on the load of the aircraft the destination city alternative departures and alternative arrivals as well as weather and the possibility for weather diversions. However company policies often dictate how much fuel a pilot will put on. In the case of many larger Aviation companies and private charters a pilot putting on more fuel is not reprimanded for the action. Though in the case of some companies if they repeatedly put on more fuel than is necessary they may receive a write-up. However in the case of smaller Charter companies that have a specific and set deals and tight operating budgets a pilot may be instructed to not put on additional fuel. And depending on the negotiations that they've made with the airport and fuel suppliers a pilot may be forced to pay out of their pocket for any additional fuel that was put on board the aircraft.
